title: Regular unique game
statement: A regular unique game on alphabet $[q]$ has a finite nonempty set of vertices. Each vertex has a finite nonempty set of neighbor occurrences, each specifying a different vertex and a permutation of $[q]$. There is a positive integer degree such that every vertex has exactly that many neighbor occurrences.
hypotheses_covered: Each vertex has a finite neighborhood
Each vertex has a nonempty neighborhood
A vertex differs from each of its neighbors
Each directed neighbor occurrence has a permutation of the alphabet
Every neighborhood has cardinality equal to the common degree
